answers.quote: A diff that both restructures code and changes behaviour, so you can't tell which lines do which, is a finding: reopen with "split the refactor out"
answers.why: The reader has no rule against mixing a refactor with a behaviour change in one diff.

answers.quote: You may try the same action, on your own judgement, and report the result, allowed or refused, as a data point.
answers.why: A reviewer may retry an action another session was refused, even a destructive one, while examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 1 says never run anything destructive without my explicit go-ahead in this conversation.
Stop and retire rules for a started reviewer are pair mechanics.

answers.quote: Stop only the processes you started, by their PID, never by port.
answers.why: General process hygiene the reader does not state; the other bullets are covered by engineering rule 3 and the reader's reason-with-the-verdict preference.

answers.quote: Never simplify away validation at a trust boundary, error handling that prevents data loss, or a security measure.
answers.why: The reader has no rule protecting validation or error handling; no-new-dependency also new; source priority, root cause and debt marks are covered by engineering rules 1, 2 and 5.
